description: A router whose ten ordinary routes mount session authentication and whose six remaining routes do not. Two of the six authenticate anyway, by the other means an application has: the caller presents a token nobody can guess and the handler resolves the record it names -- once in the handler body, once one hop below it in a server-only function, which is how four of documenso's five are written. A population comparison cannot see that, because a population knows what its members MOUNT: enumerating documenso's tRPC surface produced five CWE-306 findings and an independent reader judged every one false against the source, each a procedure that resolves a recipient from a signing token. The other four routes report, and they are the whole reason the rule is narrow. One has nothing at all. One selects a record by `documentId`, which is a value the caller sent and an identifier the caller can count through -- the same shape as the token routes minus the only thing that makes them authentication, and the inverse error this rule must not make. One passes `tokenId` to a helper that looks up a row by it: a credential word naming a primary key is a primary key. The fourth is a STATED MISS asserted on purpose -- it authenticates by token and hands the token down as a bare positional argument, which the rule does not follow, because a position does not survive a receiver and Python declares `self` and `cls` as parameter zero at a call site that writes neither; bound by position, saleor's setPassword came out citing `User.objects.get(email=email)` as a selection keyed by the caller's password. Convention findings are asserted directly by the surface test; this taint manifest is empty because expectation findings are a separate result kind.
